price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: defensive suppression (a play type being suppressed by the opponent)
adherence to the recommended mix (distance between observed and recommended mix, AVOID share)
winning at game and series level
methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict game or series wins after controlling for team and opponent strength?
Is the recommended mix derived from outcomes, including the games it is tested on?
Is a unit count of about 54 series enough to detect a plausible adherence effect?
Is the apparent effect driven by one play type (CUT) or by label construction?
How reliable are the inferred play-type and suppression labels, and how often is the suppression trigger exposed?
Is adherence a cause of winning or a marker of team quality or game state (a team that is ahead plays differently)?

historical_evidence.finding: Closest prior question: series-level AVOID share vs winning. Game-level rho=-0.19 (p=0.008), but n is inflated and confounded by team quality. Series-level rho=-0.26, p=0.07, n=50 series, underpowered; about 80 series would be needed for p<0.05. Still confounded by team quality (OKC disciplined and good). Verdict recorded as inconclusive.

Holdout games closer to the recommended mix scored higher. Raw gap +5.18 ORtg, strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual), n=908 game-team rows (454 games). The outcome is offensive efficiency, not winning. Validation is the same pipeline, no CI stated, and model regret is non-negative by construction.

System BEST beats a constrained league mix overall (1.481 vs 1.212 PPP, n=283), but the headline is CUT-driven. Non-CUT BEST vs mix gap=+0.010 (p=0.1709, n=136); L3 matchup non-CUT gap=+0.001 (p=0.3277, n=47). BEST vs AVOID gap=+0.692 (n=169). Recorded as an adequately powered null for matchup specificity, limited by selection/regression to the mean and small sample.

Execution conformance of the observed mix to the recommended opener in 4 playoff G1s (8 sides). Average |delta| 4.5 to 24.0pp. 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank 1. CUT and PNR muted by the tagger floor. No outcome comparison.

The best counter after a suppressed play type is not clearly stable across population, team and matchup levels. L1 n_mu ranges from 5 to 696 and playoff matchups from 4 to 44. Flagged for mechanical floor and sample size.
BEST share is descriptively varied by team, but win% is not identified with BEST share (IND 4.5% BEST, 71% win; DEN 4.9% BEST, 62% win; ORL AVOID 59.3%, 0% win). No inferential test.

The play-type classifier's assisted flag existed only on makes, giving SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP and TRANSITION 0.62 PPP. After the rewrite SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. Earlier play-type PPP results are exposed to this class of construction artifact.

Inferred defensive scheme labels show near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise. 99% of units show scheme change, so real adjustment cannot be separated from offense executing differently.
On-ball defensive scheme labels reached only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of confident labels in one game, and switches_on was unpopulated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level association of AVOID share with winning
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as unanswerable/underpowered: n=50 series, p=0.07, about 80 needed, confounded by team quality; game-level significance was inflated by non-independent n.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-specific (non-CUT) BEST counters beating a league mix
failed_approaches.why: Adequately powered null for non-CUT (gap +0.010, p=0.17); the headline gap was CUT-driven, with selection/regression-to-the-mean and small-sample limits.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Stable best-counter ranking from population to team to matchup
failed_approaches.why: Inconclusive: small n at matchup level and mechanical floor.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type PPP from the earlier classifier
failed_approaches.why: Assisted-flag leak (artifact): assisted flag exists only on makes, creating spurious PPP.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme changes from play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: Label noise and an inability to distinguish defensive adjustment from offensive execution.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball coverage from matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Very low confident-label rates and an unpopulated switches_on field.

evidence_establishes: The identical series-level question (adherence/AVOID share vs winning) was previously run at n=50 series and was inconclusive and confounded by team quality (FAM:SF-CHT-039).

At the game-team level, closeness to the recommended mix was associated with higher offensive efficiency after strength control (FAM:SF-APPM-001), with the caveats that validation was same-pipeline and the outcome was PPP, not wins.
Where BEST advantages were tested, they were driven by CUT; non-CUT, matchup-specific advantages were indistinguishable from a league mix (FAM:SF-APPS-023).
Series-level power for this type of test needs roughly 80 series in the earlier estimate, more than 54 (FAM:SF-CHT-039).
Play-type labels have had at least one construction artifact (FAM:SF-PAP-096), and inferred scheme labels are noisy (FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPS-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence predicts winning (as opposed to PPP) once team quality, opponent quality and game state are controlled.
Whether the efficiency association in FAM:SF-APPM-001 survives out-of-pipeline validation or is a by-product of how the recommended mix is built.
Whether the recommended mix is estimated without the test games; the records do not say.
Whether any adherence effect exists outside CUT.
Whether adherence is stable enough within a series to be a team-level trait (FAM:SF08 is descriptive only).
Anything about the 2025-26 playoffs beyond 4 G1 descriptives.
own_inferences: The question as posed ('predicts winning') most likely maps to the previously inconclusive FAM:SF-CHT-039 design, so 54 series would be only marginally larger than the prior n=50 and still below the roughly 80 needed.

A positive adherence-winning association would be expected mostly from reverse causation and talent: better or leading teams can execute the recommended mix and have more freedom to do so, and recommended-mix regret is non-negative by construction.

Game-level analysis with series clustering, team and opponent strength adjustment, and in-game score state would have more power than series-level tests but less independent information; the effective sample is still about 54 series.
The CUT-driven pattern implies that any adherence effect may reflect CUT share and the tagger floor rather than a general strategic benefit.
Unless the recommended mix is fitted strictly on prior seasons or earlier games, the test is circular.
uncertainties: How adherence is operationalized (L1 distance, AVOID share, BEST share) and whether the recommended mix is fitted with game outcomes.
Whether the 54 series include regular-season or play-in units; the data statement lists 54 series, but the 2025-26 playoffs are only partial before 2026-06-21.
How often a suppression trigger occurs per team-game, and the share of INSUFF (insufficient-data) cases, as in SF08 (DEN 70.8% INSUFF).
Whether the classifier rewrite after FAM:SF-PAP-096 is applied consistently to all seasons.
Effect size needed to be meaningful; none was recorded in the retrieved records for win outcomes.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, a direct test on 54 series might seem feasible. FAM:SF-CHT-039 shows the same question at n=50 was underpowered and talent-confounded, and FAM:SF-APPS-023 shows a CUT-driven effect that disappears for non-CUT. This moves the decision from a simple proceed to proceed_with_changes: pre-register a game-level clustered design with strength controls and an out-of-sample mix, and treat any series-only result as exploratory.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series is below the roughly 80 that FAM:SF-CHT-039 estimated for p<0.05 on a similar effect; series-level inference will likely be underpowered.
Team quality and game state drive both adherence and winning; the previous attempt was confounded and recorded as inconclusive.
If the recommended mix or BEST/AVOID labels are derived from outcomes in the evaluated games, the adherence-win link is partly built in.

prior_work.summary: The series-level version was tried at n=50 and was inconclusive and confounded (FAM:SF-CHT-039). A game-level efficiency version was supported with same-pipeline validation (FAM:SF-APPM-001). A matchup-specificity test for non-CUT counters was an adequately powered null (FAM:SF-APPS-023). No retrieved record tests adherence against winning with adequate power and out-of-sample validation.

risks.text: 54 series is underpowered at the effect size seen previously (rho about -0.26); game-level n is inflated by within-series dependence.
Team talent, opponent strength, home court, and in-game score state affect both mix adherence and winning.
BEST/AVOID rankings are derived from PPP outcomes; if fitted on the test games, adherence is partly defined by the results it predicts.
A recommended mix fitted on the full season or on games including those being predicted leaks future information.
Play-type and suppression labels are inferred from play-by-play; noisy labels attenuate or create associations (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
The tagger floor mutes CUT and PNR (FAM:SF-APPS-017), and CUT drives previous BEST gains, so adherence may be a tagger artifact.
Suppression triggers and matchup cells can be very sparse (n_mu as low as 4 to 5), and many cases are INSUFF.
Selecting best counters from small cells gives winner's-curse and regression-to-the-mean effects (FAM:SF-APPS-023).
Many adherence definitions, play-type subsets and levels (L1/L2/L3) allow forking paths.
Four seasons of rules, styles and tagger versions; the 2025-26 playoffs are only partially complete as of 2026-06-16.

design.estimand: Within-series, game-level association between pre-specified adherence (negative L1 distance between the observed post-suppression mix and a recommended mix fitted without that game or series) and the odds of winning the game, conditional on pre-game team strength, opponent strength, home court and score state. The series-level contrast is a secondary, exploratory analysis. The association is reported as predictive, not causal.
design.unit: Primary: team-game within a series, with clustering by series. Secondary: series (adherence differential between the two teams vs series winner).
design.sample: Playoff series from 2022-23 to 2024-25 as the pre-registered discovery sample (the 54 units are recorded in the task; reconcile with series counts before locking). The 2025-26 playoffs are held out and analyzed only after 2026-06-21, when complete. Exclude games with fewer than a pre-set number of trigger events or INSUFF cases, and report the exclusion counts.
design.power: Series-level (n=54): about 80 series was estimated as needed for p<0.05 at rho about -0.26 (FAM:SF-CHT-039), so the secondary test is expected to be underpowered; report the CI and minimal detectable effect and do not treat a null as evidence of no effect. Primary game-level power calculated using the intraclass correlation within series and the effective sample size, and stated before the data are examined.
design.controls: Pre-game team strength (rating prior to the series or from prior seasons), opponent strength, home court, series game number, score-state or leverage buckets, and pace; the mix is fitted only on data prior to the evaluated game (rolling or leave-one-series-out); CUT shown with and without; classifier version fixed after the FAM:SF-PAP-096 rewrite; the same label-noise audit for all seasons.
design.falsification: Placebo: replace the recommended mix by (a) a league-default mix, (b) a mix from a randomly assigned opponent trigger, and (c) shuffled adherence within team; the effect should vanish under shuffles. Non-CUT-only analysis should still show an effect (FAM:SF-APPS-023 shows non-CUT BEST advantages near zero). Negative control: adherence in games where no suppression trigger occurred. Prediction of PPP and of wins should differ in sign or magnitude only if adherence acts through efficiency.
design.multiplicity: One primary adherence metric and one primary outcome (game win, logistic with series cluster-robust SE). Secondary analyses (series-level, CUT/non-CUT split, PPP outcome) are labeled exploratory and corrected with Holm or reported with FDR. No metric changes after unblinding.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary coefficient is in the expected direction with a 95% CI excluding zero, survives the strength and score-state controls and the placebo checks, remains in the non-CUT subset with the same sign, and replicates in the held-out 2025-26 playoffs. Rejected if the CI excludes the minimal effect of interest, which must be pre-specified. Otherwise report inconclusive; do not claim a series-level result at n=54 as confirmatory.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files, play-by-play and derived play-type graph database; 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13), and 2025-26 playoffs only after completion on 2026-06-21. Freeze the classifier version, recommended-mix fitting code and the data snapshot with hashes before analysis.

research_concepts: team win prediction at series level
methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix conditional on opponent suppression predict game or series wins?
How is the recommended mix derived and is it outcome-derived or leaking look-ahead information?
Is a 54-series sample sufficient power for testing adherence effects?
How to control for team quality and confounding when testing adherence to recommendations?
How reliable are play-type labels derived from play-by-play, and what is the sparsity of suppression exposure?
args.query: suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix adherence predicts winning, best/avoid counter strategy against defensive suppression, playoff series

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

The earlier run had only 50 series with a weak correlation, so I'm noting that this 54-series setup is still confounded by team quality, while the game-level APPM-001 support rests on same-pipeline validation.

I'm working through the evidence quality for the APPS-023 and PAP-096 findings, and the question is whether a 54-series sample is enough to test the recommended-mix claim. The playoff data from 2025-26 looks only partly complete, so I'll settle on a decision to proceed with changes rather than as posed, and sketch rough probabilities for the possible outcomes before writing it up.
